newsitem.title: UK: Sexual diseases concentrate AIDS virus - study.
newsitem.headline: Sexual diseases concentrate AIDS virus - study.

text.p: Men suffering from sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) are much more likely to pass on HIV, the virus that causes AIDS, in their semen, a team of international researchers reported on Friday.
They said infection caused the virus to concentrate -- perhaps because it was preying on the immune system cells sent in to fight the STD.
Myron Cohen of the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, along with researchers in Switzerland and Malawi, said their findings added to research that STDs help spread AIDS.
"The concentration of HIV in semen is likely to be an important determinant of HIV infectiousness," they wrote in a report in the Lancet medical journal.
Cohen's team studied 206 men in Malawi who had urethritis -- an infection of the duct that carries urine, which is often caused by gonorrhea. They also studied 127 men who did not.
Half the men in both groups had HIV -- typical of men showing up for STD treatment in Malawi.
They measured how much HIV was in the semen of the men and checked to make sure they all had similar levels of the virus in their blood.
"HIV shedding in semen was eight times greater in HIV-positive men with urethritis than in the HIV-positive controls, who had similar CD4 counts and blood viral burdens," they wrote.
After being treated with antibiotics, the men who had suffered urethritis did shed less HIV, they said. Those who got no antibiotics continued to produce the same amount of virus in their semen.
"We conclude that the diagnosis and treatment of STDs, especially gonorrhea, in patients with HIV infection should be a key component of HIV prevention programmes," they wrote.
